description: Generate a slide-deck-quality Harvey ball matrix: options as rows scored against criteria as columns, every cell drawn in one style (Harvey balls 0–4 from empty to full, ticks 0/1, or 0–5 dots), with an optional highlighted 'Recommended' row, an optional notes column (appears when any row has notes) and a legend. Choose it to compare vendors, tools, plans or features side by side; use a timeline when the point is WHEN work happens, a process for ordered steps, a pyramid/funnel for a hierarchy or narrowing stages, and a hub and spoke, mind map or org chart for relationships. Limits: 2–12 rows, 1–8 criteria, row names up to 40 characters; scores outside the style's range are clamped and null leaves a cell blank. Infer missing details rather than asking; the user can adjust the chart in the builder through the Edit link. ALWAYS give the user the image link: inline chat images usually cannot be saved, but the link renders the exact chart on demand and can be pasted into a slide or Markdown.

inputSchema.description: A comparison matrix: options (rows) scored against criteria (columns) with Harvey balls, ticks or dots.

credit.description: Shows a small "twominutetoolkit.com" credit under the chart, inside the card. Set false to leave it off (for example when the user asks for no branding).

criteria.description: Column headings, left to right: what each option is scored on, e.g. ["Cost", "Ease of use", "Integrations"]. 1–8 criteria, up to 40 characters each; long names wrap to two lines.

legend.description: Show a one-line legend under the grid explaining the scale. Default true.

look.description: Drawing style, the same in every tool. "regular": clean lines and Inter (the default). "bold": heavier, slightly larger type and thicker lines, for slides read from a distance. "sketch": hand-drawn, with a handwriting font and pen lines that wobble a little, for early ideas and workshops. Use the one the user asks for; otherwise leave it out.

notes.description: Show the Notes column on the right. true shows it even when no row has a note yet; false hides it (any row notes are kept but not drawn). When omitted, the column appears automatically as soon as any row has a note, so you can simply set rows[].notes.

palette.description: Hex colours applied in order to items that have no colour of their own. Pass the user's brand colours here when they name them. Default: indigo, sky, emerald, amber, red, gray.

rows.description: The options being compared, top to bottom (2–12). Each has a name and one score per criterion, in the same order as `criteria`.

color.description: Optional hex colour for this row's balls, ticks or dots, e.g. "#10b981". Default: the first palette colour (or dark slate if that colour is too light to read).

highlight.description: Tint this row and tag it "Recommended". Use it on the option you are recommending (normally just one). Default false.

name.description: Option name shown in the left column (up to 40 characters; long names wrap to two lines).

notes.description: Optional short comment shown in the Notes column on the right (wrapped to two lines, up to 160 characters). See the top-level `notes` field for when that column appears.

scores.description: One score per criterion, in criteria order. Range depends on `style`: harvey 0–4 (0 empty ring … 4 full ball), check 0/1 (1 draws a tick), dots 0–5 (filled dots). null leaves a cell blank (drawn as a muted dash). Values outside the style's range are clamped with a warning; a shorter array leaves the remaining cells blank, a longer one is truncated.

style.description: Cell style for the whole grid: "harvey" (Harvey balls, scores 0–4 from empty to full), "check" (a tick for 1, nothing for 0) or "dots" (0–5 filled dots out of five). Default "harvey".

title.description: Heading shown top-left of the chart at 22px bold. Every chart has one title row; an empty string hides it.

width.description: Chart width in pixels (640–2400, default 1280, which suits a 16:9 slide). PNG output renders at 2x. Height is computed from the content.
